stimulus.text: The photograph shows a narrow alley between tall tenement buildings in New York City. Laundry hangs on lines overhead. Men stand in doorways and on a wooden balcony, and a man in the foreground holds a long stick. The alley floor is wet stone, with barrels at one side and a cart in the distance.
stimulus.source_note: Jacob A. Riis, “Bandits’ Roost, 59 1-2 Mulberry Street,” 1888. Photograph from the shared image pool; public domain.

source: original; stimulus verified against its source (see source_note)

books.section: Topic 6.8 Immigration and Migration in the Gilded Age

primary_sources: Jacob A. Riis, “Bandits’ Roost, 59 1-2 Mulberry Street” (1888); Jacob A. Riis, How the Other Half Lives (1890)

stem: A student claims the photograph proves that all immigrants in New York lived in crime-ridden alleys. The best answer to that claim is what?

options.text: The photograph shows no people at all in the alley
options.misconception: Denies people the photograph plainly shows.

options.text: Riis photographed only wealthy neighborhoods, not the slums
options.misconception: Puts Riis in wealthy neighborhoods he never photographed.

options.text: The alley was in Chicago, not in New York
options.misconception: Moves a New York alley to Chicago.

options.text: One alley cannot stand for every immigrant neighborhood

rationales.A: The photograph is full of people in doorways, on a balcony, and in the alley.
rationales.B: Riis photographed the poorest slums, not wealthy neighborhoods.
rationales.C: The alley is on Mulberry Street in New York, as Riis titled it.
rationales.D: A single alley shows crowding in that one place. It cannot prove how all immigrants in a city of over a million people lived.
rationales.general:
Ask how much one photograph can prove.
1. The photograph shows one alley on Mulberry Street.
2. New York held over a million people and many immigrant neighborhoods.
3. One place cannot stand for every neighborhood in a great city.
4. The photograph proves crowding there, not a single life for all immigrants.
Remember: one example proves one place, not a whole city.

figures.caption: Bandits’ Roost, Mulberry Street, New York, photographed by Jacob Riis in 1888
